query: What review signals predict negative IMDb audience satisfaction?

per_column.name: neg_word_ratio
per_column.rationale: Fraction of negative-lexicon words, derived from review_text and external to the label; a classic sentiment signal that plausibly predicts negative satisfaction.

per_column.name: pos_word_ratio
per_column.rationale: Fraction of positive-lexicon words; external to the label and carries directional sentiment signal for predicting positivity.

per_column.name: neg_minus_pos_ratio
per_column.rationale: Net sentiment balance combining the two ratios; a single directional signal plausibly correlated with the label, not a restatement of it.

per_column.name: negation_count
per_column.rationale: Count of negation tokens; captures polarity flips and modulates sentiment interpretation, a legitimate lexical predictor.

per_column.name: intensified_neg_count
per_column.rationale: Count of intensified negatives (e.g., 'very bad'); a targeted signal of strong negativity, external to the label.

per_column.name: exclamation_count
per_column.rationale: Punctuation-based intensity marker; weak but plausible affective signal, not derived from the label.

per_column.name: avg_sentence_length
per_column.rationale: Stylistic feature; only weakly related to sentiment but a legitimate, non-leaking structural predictor.

per_column.name: caps_ratio
per_column.rationale: Proportion of capitalized characters; a plausible affect/emphasis proxy, external to the label.

per_column.name: review_length_log
per_column.rationale: Log review length; a generic but legitimate structural feature that can correlate with satisfaction, no leakage.

per_column.name: negation_before_pos_count
per_column.rationale: Negation preceding positive words captures sarcasm/polarity reversal; a targeted, non-leaking sentiment predictor, though very sparse in observed values.

judge.rationale: All added columns are functions of review_text and none restate or leak the label_pos outcome, so they qualify as legitimate predictors. The set includes genuinely intent-relevant sentiment engineering (neg/pos ratios, net balance, negation handling, intensified negatives, negation-before-positive for sarcasm) that carries real signal about audience satisfaction, plus weaker generic structural features (length, caps, exclamation, sentence length). The lexicon-based sentiment features provide meaningful predictive leverage beyond the raw text, but sparsity in several counts (e.g., intensified_neg_count and negation_before_pos_count are mostly zero) and reliance on some generic features limit the overall lift, yielding moderate predictive utility.
